$comment: Which auto-compaction window each train is INTENDED to run with (spec §5.2).
The entrypoint compares this to the effective value resolved from the settings layers and
refuses on disagreement, in both directions. Too small hides context; too large silently
adopts a tier the train was never scoped to.
300000 is the ACCEPTED marathon tier — Kuya, 2026-07-31, on #19: 'accepted as Compy's scoped
marathon tier. It is not the default; routine work remains standard.' Acceptance settled the
tier's name and status, not its scoping: it is still granted per issue.
Widening `default` to the marathon tier to make a refusal go away would be exactly the failure
this file exists to prevent: a routing mistake made invisible by a setting.
2026-08-07 — `default` raised 150000 -> 250000, and this is NOT that failure. It is not a
refusal being silenced; it is the standard tier being repaired. Measured across 34 recent
sessions: auto-compaction fires at 0.77-0.80 of the window (not the 0.92-0.95 the code assumed),
so 150000 meant a hard ceiling of ~116k, while the fixed per-turn floor had grown to a p75 of
77k. 38k of working headroom refills in one or two file reads, which IS the owner's recurring
'Autocompact is thrashing' dialog. 250000 restores ~115k. Sessions before the pin existed
routinely peaked at 270-393k on this machine, so the tier ceiling is not the binding limit.
scripts/context-headroom-guard.test.mjs now fails the build if this ever narrows again.
Adding an issue here is a decision, not a fix. Record why in `note`.
